# phosphor-host-ipmid / fuzz_payload_unpack

OSS-Fuzz's fuzz target `fuzz_payload_unpack` ([source](source/fuzz_payload_unpack.cpp), unmodified) over phosphor-host-ipmid (openbmc/phosphor-host-ipmid at 3bcd5f2c).

selector%16 picks one of 16 ipmi::message::Payload pack/unpack paths (fundamental ints, fixed-width bit types, strings, vectors, optionals, arrays, bitsets, SecureBuffer, span, nested Payload, reset/re-unpack, prepend); every return code (unpack() returns int) is discarded.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against phosphor-host-ipmid at commit 3bcd5f2c with 3 patches to the library (listed on the project page).
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing, so a statement about it says only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch phosphor-host-ipmid` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.
